content.text:
The CI coverage check now passes at **91%** against the required 90%. All 114 backend tests pass and lint is clean. Nothing is committed or pushed.

## Results

| Check (same commands as CI) | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts/tests-start.sh` (runs `scripts/test.sh`) | **114 passed**, 0 failed |
| `coverage report --fail-under=90` | **91%** (828 statements, 77 not covered), passes |
| `scripts/lint.sh` (mypy, ty, ruff check, ruff format) | clean |
| `alembic check` | no differences between model and database |

The coverage threshold and the measured files are unchanged.

## Why coverage had dropped to 85%
- **The demo command had no tests:** 49 statements at 0%. It's now at 98%; only the `if __name__ == "__main__"` line isn't run.
- **The migration test pulls Alembic files into the measurement:** it runs Alembic inside the test process, so `app/alembic/**` counts toward the measured source `app`. That added about 160 statements, mostly downgrade code in the template's older migrations that never runs. I didn't exclude them, as you asked.

## New and strengthened tests
- **Demo command** (`tests/scripts/test_seed_demo_users.py`, 7 tests). They use random emails and a temporary admin, so the real admin and demo accounts are never read or changed.
  - Refuses to run outside development and creates nothing.
  - Creates missing accounts with the right role, active status and a working password.
  - On a second run, existing accounts keep the same id, password hash, role and name.
  - Reports a conflict for a wrong role, an inactive account or a different password, exits with 1, and leaves the account exactly as it was.
  - Reports a missing configured admin, or one whose password changed.
- **Own items:** each manager and member now gets one owned item and one foreign item. The test checks `count == 1`, that the list contains exactly the owned item's id, and that opening the foreign item returns 403.
  - With the item filter deliberately broken, both role variants fail, so the test catches it.
- **Admin demoted to manager by another admin, same token:**
  - Viewing the user list and a user still returns 200.
  - Creating a user, changing another user's role, deactivating a user, changing their own role back to admin, and deleting a user all return 403.
  - The database confirms nothing changed.

## A problem the full run exposed, now fixed
- **Symptom:** 4 demo command tests passed on their own but failed in the full suite.
- **Cause:** the migration test runs first, and Alembic's `env.py` calls `logging.config.fileConfig()`. That disables every logger already created in the process, so the demo command's log messages were never captured. Running the two folders in the opposite order made them pass, which confirmed it.
- **Fix:** I used Alembic's documented `configure_logger` option. `env.py` skips logging setup only when the migration test asks it to, so the `alembic` command and `prestart.sh` behave as before (checked with `alembic current`).

## State afterwards
- **Accounts:** the configured admin and both demo accounts are unchanged, and no temporary migration databases are left.
- **Leftover test users:** the backend tests clean up the users they create. The 4 users left by the earlier Playwright run are still in the database.

## No remaining failures, but not re-run in this round
- **Frontend checks:** no frontend files changed since the last round, so I didn't run frontend lint, the type check or the admin Playwright tests again (13 passed last time).
- **Other Playwright specs** are still unrun.

+### Roles and Access
+
+Users have one role: `admin` (manage users and roles, see all items), `manager` (view users and metrics) or `member` (own profile and items). Rules live in `backend/app/core/permissions.py`; the backend enforces them and returns the user's `permissions` from `/api/v1/users/me` for the frontend.
+
+To try all three roles locally, create the demo accounts (development only). They use the `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Existing accounts are never changed; mismatches are reported as conflicts:
+
+```bash
+cd backend
+uv run python -m app.seed_demo_users
+```
+
+Log in as `FIRST_SUPERUSER` (admin), `manager@example.com` or `member@example.com`.
+
+**API change:** `is_superuser` was replaced by `role` in user requests and responses. The migration turns existing superusers into admins and everyone else into members.  The frontend development server uses the backend at `http://localhost:8000`, as configured in `frontend/.env`.
 
+### Roles and Access
+
+Users have one role: `admin` (manage users and roles, see all items), `manager` (view users and metrics) or `member` (own profile and items). Rules live in `backend/app/core/permissions.py`; the backend enforces them and returns the user's `permissions` from `/api/v1/users/me` for the frontend.
+
+To try all three roles locally, create the demo accounts (development only). They use the `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Existing accounts are never changed; mismatches are reported as conflicts:
+
+```bash
+cd backend
+uv run python -m app.seed_demo_users
+```
+
+Log in as `FIRST_SUPERUSER` (admin), `manager@example.com` or `member@example.com`.
+
+**API change:** `is_superuser` was replaced by `role` in user requests and responses. The migration turns existing superusers into admins and everyone else into members. Invalid, expired, inactive or deleted sessions now return `401` (previously `403`/`400`/`404`); `403` means the user lacks permission.
+
+**Deployment order:** stop the old backend, run migrations (`scripts/prestart.sh`), then start the new backend and frontend together. The old backend cannot run against the migrated schema.
+

 The frontend development server uses the backend at `http://localhost:8000`, as configured in `frontend/.env`.
 
+### Roles and Access
+
+Users have one role: `admin` (manage users and roles, see all items), `manager` (view users and metrics) or `member` (own profile and items). Rules live in `backend/app/core/permissions.py`; the backend enforces them and returns the user's `permissions` from `/api/v1/users/me` for the frontend.
+
+To try all three roles locally, create the demo accounts (development only). They use the `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Existing accounts are never changed; mismatches are reported as conflicts:
+
+```bash
+cd backend
+uv run python -m app.seed_demo_users
+```
+
+Log in as `FIRST_SUPERUSER` (admin), `manager@example.com` or `member@example.com`.
+
+**API change:** `is_superuser` was replaced by `role` in user requests and responses. The migration turns existing superusers into admins and everyone else into members. Invalid, expired, inactive or deleted sessions now return `401` (previously `403`/`400`/`404`); `403` means the user lacks permission.
+
+**Deployment order:** stop the old backend, run migrations (`scripts/prestart.sh`), then start the new backend and frontend together. The old backend cannot run against the migrated schema.
+

The final diff is clean: no unrelated changes and no local files included by accident. I found two small nits, listed below. Nothing is committed or pushed.

## Accidental files
- **Untracked files:** only the 11 intended new files.
- **Ignored files:** only caches, build output and test artifacts: `.venv`, `node_modules`, `.coverage`, `htmlcov`, `frontend/openapi.json`, `frontend/playwright/` and `frontend/test-results/`. `frontend/playwright/` holds the saved admin login session, and git ignores it.
- **No secrets:** no `.env` copies, tokens, passwords, scratch files or launch configs are in the diff. `.git/info/exclude` is back to its original contents.
- **Whitespace:** `git diff --check` reports no problems.

## Review findings
- **Backend:** every change is about roles: permission checks, the `role` field, the 401/403 split, the self-demotion guard, the metrics stub and the demo command. `env.py` gained only the two small options for tests; the `alembic` command behaves as before.
- **Generated files:** they contain only what the generator produced from the new API: `Role`, `Permission`, `MetricsService`, and `is_superuser` removed. The route tree only adds `/metrics`.
- **`__root.tsx`:** it looks rewritten, but the code formatter just re-indented it because the root route signature got longer. The only real change is passing the query client to routes.
- **Tests:** the existing tests changed only from `is_superuser` to `role`. The new tests use throwaway data. The shared cleanup now deletes only what the tests create.

## Two small nits (not fixed)
1. **Docs wording:** `development.md` says admins "see all items". They can also edit and delete them, so "manage all items" is more accurate.
2. **Unneeded exports:** `useAuth.ts` exports `currentUserQueryOptions` and `hasPermission`, but no other file uses them. They could become private.

# FastAPI Project - Development

## Local Development

For local development, run PostgreSQL and Mailpit with Docker Compose, and run the FastAPI and Vite development servers locally.

Start the supporting services:

```bash
docker compose up -d db mailpit
```

Then, from the `backend` directory, install the dependencies and prepare the database:

```bash
uv sync
uv run bash scripts/prestart.sh
```

Start the FastAPI development server:

```bash
uv run fastapi dev
```

In another terminal, from the project root, install the frontend dependencies and start the Vite development server:

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

Now you can open these URLs:

Frontend development server: <http://localhost:5173>

Backend API: <http://localhost:8000>

Automatic interactive API documentation with Swagger UI: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

Mailpit: <http://localhost:8025>

The frontend development server uses the backend at `http://localhost:8000`, as configured in `frontend/.env`.

### Roles and Access

Users have one role: `admin` (manage users and roles, see all items), `manager` (view users and metrics) or `member` (own profile and items). Rules live in `backend/app/core/permissions.py`; the backend enforces them and returns the user's `permissions` from `/api/v1/users/me` for the frontend.

To try all three roles locally, create the demo accounts (development only). They use the `FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Existing accounts are never changed; mismatches are reported as conflicts:

```bash
cd backend
uv run python -m app.seed_demo_users
```

Log in as `FIRST_SUPERUSER` (admin), `manager@example.com` or `member@example.com`.

**API change:** `is_superuser` was replaced by `role` in user requests and responses. The migration turns existing superusers into admins and everyone else into members. Invalid, expired, inactive or deleted sessions now return `401` (previously `403`/`400`/`404`); `403` means the user lacks permission.

**Deployment order:** stop the old backend, run migrations (`scripts/prestart.sh`), then start the new backend and frontend together. The old backend cannot run against the migrated schema.

### Frontend Served by FastAPI

Build the frontend from the `frontend` directory:

```bash
bun run build
```

The build is written to `backend/app/frontend` and served by FastAPI at <http://localhost:8000>. Rebuild the frontend after making frontend changes.

## Full Stack with Docker Compose

To run the backend and built frontend in Docker Compose:

```bash
docker compose run --rm backend bash scripts/prestart.sh
docker compose watch
```

Now you can open these URLs:

Application, with the frontend and API served by FastAPI: <http://localhost:8000>

Automatic interactive API documentation with Swagger UI: <http://localhost:8000/docs>

Adminer, database web administration: <http://localhost:8080>

Traefik UI, to see how the routes are being handled by the proxy: <http://localhost:8090>

Mailpit: <http://localhost:8025>

Stop a locally running FastAPI server before starting the Compose backend because both use port `8000`.

**Note**: The first time you start the stack, it might take a minute for all the services to be ready. To monitor it, use `docker compose logs`, or `docker compose logs backend` for the backend service.

## Mailpit

[Mailpit](https://mailpit.axllent.org) captures emails sent during local development instead of delivering them. The local backend connects to it at `localhost:1025`, and the Compose backend connects to the `mailpit` service. Captured emails are available at <http://localhost:8025>.

## Docker Compose Files and Environment Variables

The main `compose.yml` file contains the configuration shared by the whole stack. Docker Compose loads it automatically.

The `compose.override.yml` file adds local development settings, such as mounting the source code as a volume. Docker Compose also loads it automatically and applies it on top of `compose.yml`.

The `compose.deploy.yml` file contains the deployment-specific settings, including HTTPS and automatic certificate handling. It is explicitly combined with `compose.yml` when deploying the application.

The backend reads local settings from the `.env` file. Docker Compose also uses it for variable interpolation and passes the settings each container needs.

After changing variables, make sure you restart the stack:

```bash
docker compose watch
```

## The `.env` File

The tracked `.env` file contains local development defaults, passwords, and other configuration. Its hostnames use `localhost` for processes running on your machine. Docker Compose overrides hostnames such as the database and SMTP server with their Compose service names.

Do not store deployment secrets in `.env`. Configure them as described in the [FastAPI Cloud deployment guide](./deployment.md) or the [Docker Compose deployment guide](./deployment-docker-compose.md).

## Pre-commit Hooks and Code Linting

The project uses [prek](https://prek.j178.dev/), a modern alternative to [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/), for code linting and formatting.

You can find a file `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with configurations at the root of the project.

### Install `prek` to Run Automatically

`prek` is already part of the dependencies of the project.

From the project root, install the Git hook so that `prek` runs automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv run prek install -f
```

The `-f` flag forces the installation, in case there was already a `pre-commit` hook previously installed.

Now whenever you try to commit, for example with:

```bash
git commit
```

`prek` will check and format the code you are about to commit. If it modifies any files, add those files to Git again before committing.

### Run `prek` Manually

You can also run `prek` manually on all files from the project root:

```bash
uv run prek run --all-files
```

The implementation is committed locally on `feature/role-based-access` and nothing is pushed.

**Commit:** `63d6c7558085f32621c6c7c9de85f1dff2e6afb0` (`63d6c75`)

- `development.md` now says admins "manage all items", plus the line: *"Time spent: approximately 1.5 hours, including local environment setup."*

- **Frontend:** permission-based menus and route guards, refreshing the current user after a 403, logout after a 401, clearing cached data when accounts switch, the role picker, the Metrics page, and the regenerated API client and route tree.
- **Tests:** the role matrix, existing sessions, escalation attempts, the null-role regression, the isolated migration test, the demo command tests and the updated admin Playwright spec.
- **Docs:** the roles section, the API change, the deployment order and the time note.

**Working tree:** clean, with nothing left uncommitted. Only git-ignored caches, build output and test artifacts remain locally. The branch isn't pushed and has no remote branch yet.
